items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: The interviewee discusses Jelly Roll Morton extensively but explicitly states 'I never knew him personally'. The name 'Arvin' is mentioned by the interviewer solely as a third party ('for Arvin to play something now') with no interaction or relationship described between the interviewee and Arvin.

ctx.x: Earl Hines, and you mentioned one of your favorites was Jess Stacy, who also was one of my favorites. And then I had so many, like Joe Sullivan, you know, and Bob Surkey, and oh, I can't hear that. You had an avalanche of great pianists, you know. I mean, so many, so many good ones. And they all were a little bit different styles, you know. Well, who's influenced your style the most? Or do you see yourself as having a certain style? I have to say now that, that in later years, in later years, I've turned more,…
Uh-huh. That's the only way I can put it. Uh-huh. Well, can, maybe, do, do we have enough tape there to, for Arvin to play something now, or is he gonna?

Well, I'd say there's about a half a minute left on here. Oh. The light's not very clear. All right, well, let's wait then. I'd like to call him to work, you know. All right, go ahead. If you've got a, sure. Now, this machine will turn itself. All right. And then, all right, when you get back, we'll, we'll play a little. All right.
